_comment: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN TWO WRITERS IN TWO LANGUAGES.
`infra/seed_cases.py` writes case records from Python and
`web/app/api/case/new/route.ts` writes them from TypeScript. Two writers
agreeing by memory is how a submitted case ends up unparseable to the agent
that has to read it — the case renders on the dashboard and Grace never sees
it, which is the exact 'looks like it works' failure Plan 4 exists to close.
So both sides assert against this one item instead of against each other:
`tests/test_case_record.py` on the Python side and
`web/__tests__/intake.test.ts` on the TypeScript side. Either writer drifting
fails its own test.
The case id is c-901 rather than one of the twelve, and there is no name,
phone, address, or email anywhere in it — a record row carries none, by
construction rather than by filtering (hard rule 9). All data is synthetic
(hard rule 3).
`created_at` is pinned so the item is byte-comparable; both writers take it
as a parameter for exactly that reason. `created_by` is pinned for the same
reason, and it is a synthetic opaque Cognito `sub` — a UUID. It says WHO
asserted this record's document status, because Grace takes a caseworker's
word that a document was sent to the state and cannot verify it. It is never
a name or an email: both writers refuse a value that is not opaque, rather
than stripping it (hard rule 9). A record seeded from the fixture carries
`{"NULL": true}` here, because nobody asserted anything about it.

L.S: household size 4 on application, 3 on most recent wage record
